reuse.why: Uses existing extractTagsFromText, getSheetValue, isTrackingBudget, batchMessages and the undoable/mutator wiring, and all bulk actions share the new getMonthWideCategories; the sign inversion of averages is not reused for the new action.

duplication.why: The three copies of the category query are collapsed, but the income-outside-tracking check stays copied in every caller (and is copied again in setLastMonthSpending) and the expense sign flip is rewritten as `0 - net`.

placement.why: Selection lives in budget/actions.ts next to the actions and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts like its siblings.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the bulk actions, the new method registration and tests for the four steps.

maintainability.why: One helper owns the hidden/template/#fixed rules with a single boolean parameter, but part of the category rule (income in tracking budgets) still lives at each call site and copyPreviousMonth combines its own row query with an eligibility set.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All bulk actions, including copyPreviousMonth and the new setLastMonthSpending, use getMonthWideCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending's `cat.is_income === 0 ? 0 - net : net` reshapes the `if (is_income === 0) avg *= -1` sign inversion of set3MonthAvg/setNMonthAvg instead of sharing it.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideCategories gained only the includeHiddenCategories parameter (with its SQL hidden-filter branch) required by step 4; every bulk action calls it, though each still applies the income rule itself.
